facts.raw_span: progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws
symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
intact, bluish-gray oral mucosa
no lymphadenopathy
routine hematologic tests were unremarkable
well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas involving the mandibular bodies, angles, ascending rami, and the maxillary tuberosities
bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of the cortical plates of the maxilla and mandible

no cortical breaches or soft-tissue extension
Vital signs were normal

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws, symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla, and radiographic findings of well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas are consistent with Cherubism.

The radiographic findings of multilocular radiolucent areas and expansile lesions with thinning of the cortical plates are consistent with Central giant cell granuloma, and the mild anterior displacement of an unerupted first molar could be a result of the lesion's growth.

The patient's presentation of progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws and radiographic findings of well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas could be consistent with Fibrous dysplasia, although the symmetrical involvement is less typical.

rationales.F09: The absence of cortical breaches or soft-tissue extension suggests a slower-growing, possibly benign process.
